description: String deduplication pool for .NET that returns one canonical string instance per equal value, so repeated reads share memory and become reference-equal. Time-based eviction with configurable minRetention and maxLength. Includes System.Text.Json and Newtonsoft.Json converters for zero-effort deserialization dedup. Not based on String.Intern or WeakReference. Inspired by Go's unique package. .NET 9+.
rules: minRetention is a lower bound, not an upper bound: a value stays reference-equal for at least minRetention after last access and is evicted between minRetention and 2x minRetention — the opposite of MemoryCache/Caffeine expiry semantics, deliberate for canonicalization.
Reuse one UniqueStringPool per logical domain; worst-case live entry count is bounded by unique inserts during 2x minRetention, and per-entry cost is bounded by maxLength (default 256).
Use the ReadOnlySpan<char> overload of Make for zero-allocation lookup of already-pooled values.
UniqueStringConverter (System.Text.Json) and UniqueJsonStringConverter (Newtonsoft.Json) canonicalize on read and pass writes through unchanged — safe to attach to round-trip serializer options.
The System.Text.Json converter's stack buffer defaults to 256 chars with a 1024-char hard ceiling; raise stackBufferLength only when the pool's MaxLength is higher and a benefit is measured.

Requires .NET 9+ (relies on ConcurrentDictionary/FrozenDictionary GetAlternateLookup<ReadOnlySpan<char>>); Dodo.Unique depends on the BCL only, Dodo.Unique.NewtonsoftJson adds the Newtonsoft.Json converter.
